items.title: How to Script a YouTube Video: 5 Prompt Details to Include
items.primaryKeyword: how to script a YouTube video
items.script: Need a YouTube video prompt that gives you something usable? Don't start with “make it cinematic.” Give the prompt five anchors. One: the subject. Two: the action or lesson the viewer should see. Three: the setting and time of day. Four: the shot size and camera movement. Five: the format, duration and limits. For wildlife, add a safety rule: observe from a distance, never stage or disturb an animal, and don't invent behaviour the footage cannot support. Then request separate shot-list and narration drafts so you can fact-check every claim. A prompt is a brief, not a rights licence. The Full Video Creation Prompt Pack Premium Edition is linked below as a planning resource.

items.title: YouTube Growth Strategy: Build a 90-Day Content Plan
items.script: Want a YouTube growth strategy you can actually review? Build a 90-day plan in three blocks. Days 1–14: choose one audience problem, audit your existing videos, and write down a realistic production capacity. Days 15–60: publish a repeatable series at a pace you can sustain. For every video, record the topic, viewer promise, and one metric to review. Days 61–90: compare patterns—click-through rate, average view duration, and returning viewers—then keep what the evidence supports and change one thing at a time. Don't treat one upload as proof of a trend. A 90-day plan is a learning cycle, not a guarantee of growth. The YouTube Success Blueprint 90-Day Creator System is linked below as a planning resource.
